summary: EarthWatch is a lightweight geospatial application designed to help users explore surface changes using observations from the NASA–ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) mission. Users search for a location, draw an area of interest, choose two observation dates, and request a comparison. The React and MapLibre interface presents the selected area, observation details, and before/after views. A Node.js and Express backend validates geometry, searches official data catalogs, manages Earthdata authentication, and coordinates processing. Python-based geospatial tools prepare compatible radar observations, run an appropriate change-detection method, and produce a georeferenced change mask. Results focus on essential information: the observation pair, detected changed area, percentage of the selected area affected, data provenance, and method limitations. EarthWatch is designed to report when suitable observations are unavailable rather than fabricate results or silently substitute another sensor. Its initial demonstration focuses on flood and surface-water change, with a modular architecture that can support additional surface-change applications.
details: EarthWatch is a lightweight geospatial application—developed using a React and MapLibre frontend, a Node.js and Express backend, and Python-based data processing tools—that allows users to seamlessly explore surface changes using NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) observations. Creatively combining a highly accessible user interface with strict scientific integrity, the platform transparently manages Earthdata authentication and official catalog searches to provide precise change detection data, explicitly reporting when suitable observations are unavailable rather than fabricating results. Guided by considerations of reliability, modularity, and data provenance, the project's initial impact focuses on monitoring flood and surface-water changes, though its flexible architecture ensures it can easily expand to support a wide variety of additional surface-change applications in the future.
